correctness.rationale: For odd n≥5 the circulant Fourier symbol of P(p) is 1-pλ_k, so the exact two-round SLEM is max_k |(1-pλ_k)(1-qλ_k)|. With a=min positive Laplacian eigenvalue and b=max, the endpoint objective bounds the full spectrum. If either p<1/b, its slow endpoint is strictly too high. Otherwise with x=bp-1,y=bq-1 in [0,B], B=b/2-1, fixing c=xy and applying (B-x)(B-y)≥0 forces one factor to p=1/2 at optimum. Balancing slow and high endpoints uniquely gives the unordered pair {1/2,1/(a+b-2)} and value (2-a)(b-2)/(2(a+b-2)). For this pair the only possible intermediate magnitude excursion is a negative quadratic trough at most 1/24, smaller than the attained endpoint maximum (≥1/6). The repeated one-step optimum balances affine spectral endpoints at p=2/(a+b); direct algebra yields the positive exact gap and n^-6 expansion. Independent spectral-mode calculations for odd n=5,7,9,13,19,51,101 corroborate all finite formulas; they are not a substitute for the endpoint/trough proof.
residual_risks: No generalization to vertex-dependent or longer-range factors, even cycles, or more than two rounds.

value.rationale: The two-round fastest stochastic consensus problem with independent stage choices and a per-round nonnegative Markov constraint is a natural finite-time optimization, not covered by optimizing one stationary transition matrix. The exact pair, uniqueness and n^-6 strict improvement are useful despite the gain being asymptotically small: they distinguish feasible Markov-factor schedules from unconstrained polynomial filters. The result does not claim Chebyshev-order acceleration.
residual_risks: No generalization to vertex-dependent or longer-range factors, even cycles, or more than two rounds.
